steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Earthquakes occur when stress builds up at plate boundaries and is suddenly released as seismic waves

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The focus is the point underground where the earthquake originates; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Volcanoes form where magma reaches the surface: at divergent boundaries (fissure eruptions), subduction zones (explosive stratovolcanoes), and hotspots (shield volcanoes)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Effusive eruptions produce fluid basaltic lava (e.g. Iceland); explosive eruptions produce viscous andesitic/rhyolitic lava, ash and pyroclastic flows (e.g. Mt St Helens)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Focus vs epicentre: focus = underground, epicentre = on the surface directly above Magma type determines eruption style: basaltic = gentle, andesitic/rhyolitic = explosive Both earthquake and volcanic hazards are examined, know at least 3 of each Plate boundary type determines volcano type: divergent = shield, convergent = stratovolcano
